card.title: Still a Good Sign
card.instruction: Treat every awkward or disappointing interaction as proof that the connection remains alive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our first dinner since the breakup, and you still groan at my waiter joke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered. We've still got our little traditions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we eat in silence? I don't want another awful joke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You still know how to ask me for what you need. I'll order dessert so we have time.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 groaning marks continued familiarity, A3 dislike becomes shared tradition and A5 silence request becomes trust in expressing needs.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 hoped joke retired causes A3 remembered-tradition claim; B4 no jokes causes A5 need-sharing interpretation and dessert.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 plausibly express irritation at a repeated joke rather than provide artificial emotional cues.

heightening.evidence: B4 disappointing limit becomes A5 evidence of connection and a reason to extend time without promising more jokes.

specificity.evidence: A1 first dinner since breakup establishes why awkward familiarity matters.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 dessert for time converts the positive interpretation into a concrete continued encounter.
